scope: Synthetic authentication state-machine callback isolation; no real login or quota

defect.before: Login completion had no attempt identity; a callback from an old terminal could complete a new home login or cancel a retry, and duplicate starts were accepted.

invariants: Each attempt has a unique in-memory ID and immutable executable/home configuration
A repeated start cannot replace a running login
Only the matching active attempt can complete or cancel sign-in
Stop and reconfiguration invalidate old attempts, including same-home retries
An accepted completion is consumed before any asynchronous quota verification
Exit zero still requires a fresh successful quota response
Stale or duplicate callbacks do not launch additional quota probes
Authentication does not rewrite local history or source freshness

appHosted.overlap: The 51 integration and 18 derived cases also run in Foundation; these are not additive unique test totals.
appHosted.warnings: Existing actor-isolation and optional-coercion warnings remain outside this change.

remaining: Safe official billing startup and authenticated quota fixture
Official terminal controller and real login/cancel/timeout/logout lifecycle
Actual Dock, keyboard/VoiceOver, real sleep/wake and wider live attribution verification
Long-term retention stress, final identity asset and complete release regression/package gates
